source_findings: Reinspection covers all three printed lines of verse 7 in pdf42.png and pdf42-body.png. The candidate is a plausible reading, but I cannot confidently certify every letter of its first word, ወትሰጥም, from these photographs. The lexical proposal does not resolve that remaining visual uncertainty.
The second line supports the proposed destruction clause rather than the earlier, fallible frozen transcription. That earlier transcription is not authoritative evidence against the candidate.
The printed star before ላዕለ is real and must remain. Raised apparatus numbers 5, 6, 7 and 8 are not source-text characters.
The candidate's final ። requires checking: the photograph appears to show ፡ before raised apparatus number 8. An exact transcription cannot silently normalize this punctuation.
Charles's printed text and apparatus constitute evidence for a selected editorial reading, not independent certification of ancient manuscript wording.
English_findings: Dillmann column 400 includes the Latin sense “demergi, submergi, aquis hauriri vel obrui” and explicitly cites Hen. 1, 7. This supports sinking or submergence as a lexical possibility, but does not by itself certify the candidate's exact printed verb.
The earth clause and the following singular collective subject are represented appropriately by “The earth” and “everything.” The destruction clause is affirmative; no negation has been introduced.

Dillmann's destruction vocabulary on columns 19–20 supports perishing or destruction. “Will be destroyed” expresses the proposed clause's result, although the precise headword-to-inflected-form identification must not be replaced by a neighboring entry's meaning.
Dillmann column 217 supports the terrestrial sense of ምድር, and columns 1365–1366 support judgment language for ፍትሕ.
“Judgment will come upon all” preserves the universal scope. “Come” is an idiomatic rendering of the proposed ይከውን clause, not a separately printed motion verb.
explanation_findings: The footnote's sinking interpretation has genuine support in the photographed Latin lexicon, including its explicit Enoch reference. That reference cannot be used circularly to supply an uncertain source letter.
The English does not add a flood or a prediction about modern geography. The destruction and universal-judgment clauses remain represented.
The contrast with an “inherited rent-asunder transcription” cannot be independently verified from the supplied material.

The source note asserts inspection of pages 40 and 44, a full-chapter nine-unit ledger, twelve lexical photographs, and a particular prior-review sequence. Those provenance claims are not established by the photographs and frozen observation supplied for this bounded review.
The note appropriately distinguishes Charles's editorial apparatus from a new manuscript, but its broader author-pass claims are not evidence authorizing acceptance.
rationale: Hold the exact whole payload. The sinking proposal has primary lexical support, and the English broadly follows the proposed clauses, subjects and polarity. Nevertheless, unresolved visual certification of the first verb, an apparent final-punctuation discrepancy, and unsupported claims in the source note prevent acceptance of the entire exact submission. No alternative transcription or translation has been silently adopted.
limits: This is a candidate-facing review of the supplied verse-7 photographs, five lexicon photographs, English and explanatory claims. It does not establish unseen-page inspection, a complete-chapter ledger, ancient manuscript agreement, or approval of any person, chapter, book, artwork or publication.
